indicators.text: IODA BGP reachable prefixes or active-probing responsiveness drops >=25% below the 7-day rolling baseline for >=30 minutes.
indicators.rule: drop_pct >= 25.0 and duration_minutes >= 30

indicators.text: Two or more countries sharing a submarine cable corridor experience concurrent BGP/probing drops >=20% within a 2-hour window.
indicators.rule: shared_corridor_countries >= 2 and drop_pct >= 20.0

indicators.text: OONI measurement aggregation shows confirmed blocking or anomaly rate >=15% across >=50 daily measurements in a country.
indicators.rule: anomaly_rate >= 0.15 and measurement_count >= 50

indicators.text: Single-probe or darknet-only drop with stable BGP prefix count and normal OONI reachability.
indicators.rule: bgp_drop_pct < 5.0 and probing_drop_pct >= 25.0

indicators.text: Cross-program tip: Elements seismic/volcanic alert or Wake vessel loitering anomaly within 50 km of a submarine cable corridor.
indicators.rule: tip_distance_km <= 50

indicators.text: A watched provider network (AS14593 Starlink, AS16509 Amazon, AS8075 Microsoft, AS15169 Google, AS396982 Google Cloud) shows an IODA BGP or active-probing drop >=5% below the median of the 7 days before, over >=30 minutes. The window is IODA's own outage events on that network in the last 24 h, else the longest run of points >=5% low in the last 24 h, else the last 3 h.
indicators.rule: max(bgp_drop_pct, probing_drop_pct) >= 5.0 and window_minutes >= 30

indicators.text: A provider lists an open incident on its own status feed (AWS Health Dashboard RSS, Google Cloud and Google Workspace incidents.json, Azure status RSS, Microsoft 365's public status page, Apple System Status, Cloudflare Status, Akamai's and Zoom's incident history RSS, Slack Status, Starlink's Statuspage). Reported by the provider; Blackout does not assess its cause.
indicators.rule: provider status feed lists the incident as open (AWS: latest update not 'Service is operating normally'; Google Cloud and Google Workspace: no end; Azure: listed; Microsoft 365: status not Available, Service restored, False positive or Post-incident report published; Statuspage JSON: status not resolved, and for Cloudflare only when rated major or critical or on a network, CDN, DNS, WARP or data-centre component; Statuspage history RSS (Akamai, Zoom): newest update not Resolved, Postmortem or Completed, maintenances and Akamai's Customer Security Advisories left out; Apple: eventStatus not resolved, completed or upcoming, Maintenance left out, one incident per messageId; Slack: status not resolved, scheduled, completed or cancelled)

indicators.text: Two or more different watched providers start a BO-IND-6 drop or a BO-IND-7 incident within 2 hours of each other, inside the last 24 hours.
indicators.rule: distinct providers with onset in the last 24 h whose onsets fall within 2 h of each other >= 2

indicators.text: Cloudflare Radar's Outage Center lists an outage (annotated by Cloudflare's analysts from Cloudflare's own traffic, with the cause and type Cloudflare states), ongoing or ended within the last 72 h. Reported by Cloudflare; Blackout does not assess its cause.
indicators.rule: annotation in Radar's annotations/outages (7-day range) with no end, or an end within 72 h; cause mapped to a hypothesis: government-directed BO-H-1A supports; power outage or military action BO-H-1B supports; cable cut BO-H-2A supports; any other stated cause BO-H-1A refutes; none or unknown BO-H-1A neutral

indicators.text: Cloudflare Radar flags a traffic anomaly in its own traffic that Cloudflare has verified and no outage annotation covers, ongoing or ended within the last 72 h. Radar gives no cause.
indicators.rule: Radar traffic_anomalies (7-day range) with status TP or VERIFIED, outageId null, and no end or an end within 72 h; BO-H-1A neutral

indicators.text: Cloudflare Radar's BGP hijack detection lists an origin hijack at Cloudflare's high confidence (8 or above) seen by at least 25 of its route-collector peers, ongoing or last seen within 72 h. Reported by Cloudflare; Blackout does not assess intent.
indicators.rule: bgp/hijacks/events (3-day range, minConfidence=8) with peer_ip_count >= 25 and max_hijack_ts within 72 h; BO-H-4A neutral (routing data alone doesn't tell intent from error)

indicators.text: Cloudflare Radar's route-leak detection lists a provider-customer-provider leak of at least 100 prefixes seen by at least 25 of its route-collector peers, ongoing or finished within 72 h. Reported by Cloudflare; Blackout does not assess intent.
indicators.rule: bgp/leaks/events (3-day range) with prefix_count >= 100 and peer_count >= 25, not finished or max_ts within 72 h; grouped by leaking network; BO-H-4A neutral

indicators.text: The IAEA's newest numbered Ukraine update says the Zaporizhzhya Nuclear Power Plant is without off-site power or relies on a single off-site line (before the war it had ten). Reported by the IAEA and quoted; Blackout does not assess it.
indicators.rule: newest update read (IAEA Top News RSS for the number; text from the Wayback Machine's first capture): a sentence naming the ZNPP says it remains without off-site power (state none) or names its single, sole or only external, off-site or back-up line (state single); present for none or single, no_data when no update read states it; overdue when the newest update is more than 10 days old

indicators.text: ODIN's reporting utilities show more than 50,000 meters without power in a US state (the size of loss form DOE-417 makes reportable). Reported by the utilities through ODIN; only utilities that report to ODIN are counted. Blackout does not assess the cause.
indicators.rule: ODIN /odi?view=county read at collection: metersAffected summed by state (county FIPS to state through the Census 2025 Gazetteer); present when the sum is more than 50,000 (DOE-417 criterion 12: more than 50,000 customers out for 1 hour or more). One reading, not an hour; meters, not customers.

indicators.text: A watched city's night radiance (NASA Black Marble, moon- and surface-corrected) on its newest clear night is 40% or more below the median of its clear nights in the 14 before. Blackout's measurement; it does not say why the city is darker.
indicators.rule: per city, a box of +-0.2 degrees latitude (about 44 km square); pixels with Mandatory_Quality_Flag 0 and QF_Cloud_Mask confident or probably clear; a night counts when at least 60% of the box is clear; present when the newest counted night, at most 3 days old, is at least 40% below the median of at least 5 counted nights in the 14 before it, and that median is at least 1.0 nW/cm2/sr (a city darker than that is reported as too dark to measure a drop)

indicators.text: A US balancing authority's hourly demand, as it reports it to EIA (EIA-930), runs 25% or more below what its own day-ahead forecast usually implies (further, where its forecasts often miss) for 3 hours in a row or more. Reported by the balancing authority; Blackout measures the gap and does not assess why.
indicators.rule: per balancing authority with a median day-ahead forecast of 1,000 MW or more (EIA's 14 regional sums left out): skip its 2 newest hours; window = the 24 hours before them; its own range = the ratio of demand to day-ahead forecast in the 168 hours before the window (at least 120), median m and 1st percentile p1; an hour is low when demand/forecast / m - 1 <= -max(0.25, 1.5 * (1 - p1/m)); present when 3 or more consecutive hours in the window are low

indicators.text: The FAA's Air Traffic Control System Command Center (ATCSCC) issues a ground stop for every airport, for a whole airline, at a carrier's request at two or more airports within 2 hours, or at an airport where it names an equipment or communications outage as the condition. Reported by the FAA; Blackout does not assess its cause.
indicators.rule: ATCSCC advisories of the last 2 UTC days (fly.faa.gov advisory database), ground stops only: national = issued by DCC with NATIONAL or NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP in its title, or destination ALL with every facility included; airline = the title names an airline's ICAO code before GROUND STOP (as on 19 Jul 2024); carrier request = comments say CARRIER REQUEST, counted per airline named (else unnamed) when 2 or more airports are stopped within 2 h (as on 6 Aug 2025); equipment = impacting condition or reason names EQUIPMENT or COMMUNICATION. Weather, volume, staffing, runway and construction stops are left out. Kept while in effect and for 24 h after its effective time ends or a cancellation advisory is issued.

indicators.text: Public Bluesky posts naming a watched US service with "down" or "outage" surge: at least 30 in the 6 hours to the run and at least 5 times that service's usual for 6 hours over the 7 days before. Reported by the public, not confirmed by the company; Blackout does not assess its cause.
indicators.rule: For each name on bluesky.WATCH, hitsTotal from Bluesky's public searchPosts (api.bsky.app, no account) for '"<name>" down' plus '"<name>" outage' in the 6 hours to the run, against the same two terms over the 7 days before the window scaled to 6 hours (the usual taken as at least 4). Surge: 30 or more matches and 5 or more times the usual. Counts only; no post, text or author is kept.

indicators.text: News headlines naming a watched US service with an outage word surge in GDELT's Global Knowledge Graph: at least 5 headlines from at least 3 outlets in the 6 hours to GDELT's newest file and at least 5 times that service's usual over the 7 days before. Reported by the press, not confirmed by the company; Blackout does not assess its cause.
indicators.rule: Every GKG 2.1 15-minute file (data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv2) of the 6 hours to the newest: page titles matching a name's pattern on gdelt.WATCH and an outage word (gdelt.OUTAGE), each article URL once, against the same name's headlines per file over the 7 days of files before the window scaled to the window's 24 files (the usual taken as at least 1). Surge: 5 or more headlines, 3 or more outlets, and 5 or more times the usual. Outlet domains and links are published, never headline text.

indicators.text: NetBlocks, an internet observatory, posts a report on its public Bluesky account naming a place, platform or network with a disruption, within the last 72 hours. Reported by NetBlocks; Blackout quotes it and does not assess its cause.
indicators.rule: Every post on NetBlocks' Bluesky account (netblocks.org, its own posts and its own thread replies, not reposts), read in full each run; an item for each post of the last 72 h naming a country (its hashtags, or country names when it uses none), a platform or a network. Fields parsed from NetBlocks' words: label (Confirmed, Update, Note, ICYMI), regions, cause words, services, AS numbers and the level it states. Cable cause BO-WP-2/BO-H-2A, power or strike BO-WP-1/BO-H-1B, shutdown or restriction BO-WP-1/BO-H-1A, a platform or no country BO-WP-3/BO-H-3B; always direction neutral.

indicators.text: A satellite network's request volume on Cloudflare Radar (a network in the register's satellite-internet or maritime-and-aviation class, worldwide; Starlink also in each of its top 20 countries) is under 70% of its normal for the same weekday and hours on two runs in a row (8 h or more). The measure is the network's own traffic as Cloudflare sees it, not its users, and a level under 100% can be a holiday, an event or a routing change; it is not an outage.
indicators.rule: mean of the last 6 full hours < 70% of the median, over the 4 weeks before, of the mean of the same 6 clock hours on the same weekday, and the same one 4 h earlier. Never flagged, and named: a series with more than 5% of points at zero or under 50 distinct levels (sparse), fewer than 3 of the 4 weeks with every hour (no normal), or a normal under 20 counts an hour (coarse: a 30% dip is then within counting noise). After 72 h below the line the item is a standing condition (tier routine). Held, named and never flagged: any hour from the drop's start to now when all of Radar's traffic worldwide is under 85% of the median of the same hour 1-4 weeks earlier (state radar_wide), or when that control cannot be read (state no_control, a problem on the satcom lane). When a country series fires, all of that country's traffic over the same hours is read; under 85% of its normal, the item says so with the figure, and this never changes its direction or suppresses it. Direction neutral, hypothesis BO-H-3A not assessed.

indicators.text: Starlink's (AS14593) worldwide request volume on Cloudflare Radar is under 60% of its normal for that hour, in any of the last 6 hours, while all of Radar's traffic is not down. One hour is enough. The measure is the network's own traffic as Cloudflare sees it, not its users; it is not called an outage and no cause or likelihood is given. The 60% line was chosen on the same five known events it was tested on and needs a forward check.
indicators.rule: any of the last 6 full hours < 60% of the median of the same hour 1-4 weeks earlier, needing at least 3 of the 4 weeks and at least 100 Radar counts in the normal. Held, named and never flagged: any hour from the first hour under the line to now when all of Radar's traffic worldwide is under 85% of its own normal (radar_wide), or when that control cannot be read (no_control). Starlink worldwide only: in the replay the same reading gave 133 episodes across Starlink's countries and 40 on other networks, none of those 40 with an independent report. Direction neutral, hypothesis BO-H-3A not assessed.

warning_problems.title: State-directed internet shutdown or curfews
warning_problems.watch_condition: National or mobile ASN BGP/probing drop >=25% or OONI anomaly surge >=15% during unrest, elections, or military operations.
warning_problems.issue_on_change: Issue a warning item when BGP/probing drop crosses 40% or when OONI blocking + IODA routing drop co-occur.
warning_problems.deactivation: BGP visibility and active probing return within 10% of the 7-day baseline for 24 hours.

hypotheses.title: Deliberate state-ordered connectivity curfew or ASN shutdown
Physical power-grid failure or kinetic strike on telecom exchanges
Measurement artefact or upstream transit reroute without user blackout

warning_problems.title: Submarine cable cut or landing-station disruption
warning_problems.watch_condition: Concurrent connectivity degradation in two or more countries served by the same submarine cable corridor.
warning_problems.issue_on_change: Issue a warning item when >=2 corridor countries drop >=20% or when an outage co-occurs with an Elements seismic event or Wake maritime anomaly.
warning_problems.deactivation: Traffic reroutes restore >90% baseline connectivity or cable repair completes.

hypotheses.title: Physical submarine cable fault (anchor drag, trawler, or seabed slide)
Coordinated domestic throttling across neighbouring states
Upstream Tier-1 transit peering dispute or collector artefact

warning_problems.title: Provider-level outage at a major cloud, content or satellite internet provider
warning_problems.watch_condition: A watched provider network drops >=5% in IODA BGP or active probing (BO-IND-6), or a provider lists an open incident on its own status feed (BO-IND-7).
warning_problems.issue_on_change: Publish each drop and each open incident as an observation. A judgment on cause or spread needs this program's own measurement (BO-IND-6) and the provider's report together; claims of 'cascading' outages are tested against BO-IND-8.
warning_problems.deactivation: The provider's network returns within 5% of its 7-day median and its status feed no longer lists the incident.

hypotheses.title: Network-level outage at the provider: its routes or address space become unreachable from outside
Service or application outage at the provider without loss of network reachability (for example a cloud region or Microsoft 365 failure with an internal cause)
Concurrent outages at several providers (a shared cause or a cascade between them)
Measurement artefact (IODA collector or prober fault) or an unsupported claim, with no outage at the provider

warning_problems.title: Routing integrity: a BGP origin hijack or route leak that can divert or blackhole a network's traffic
warning_problems.watch_condition: Cloudflare Radar's BGP detection lists a high-confidence origin hijack (BO-IND-11) or a large route leak (BO-IND-12) seen widely across its route collectors.
warning_problems.issue_on_change: Publish each widely seen hijack, and each network's large leaks, as observations reported by Cloudflare. Intent is never assessed from routing data alone; a judgment needs a second line, such as an IODA drop on the victim network, OONI blocking of the same destination, or the operator's own statement.
warning_problems.deactivation: Radar stops seeing the event (no update for 72 h) or marks the leak finished more than 72 h ago.

hypotheses.title: Deliberate hijack or leak to intercept, censor or disrupt the victim's traffic (state or criminal)
Operator error: a mistyped origin, or a customer or peer exporting routes it should not (the usual case)
Legitimate change the detector misreads: sibling or customer origins, DDoS scrubbing, a move not yet in RPKI or IRR

warning_problems.title: Loss of grid power to a population or to a nuclear site
warning_problems.watch_condition: Cloudflare names a power outage as the cause of an internet outage (BO-IND-9), the IAEA reports the Zaporizhzhya NPP on one off-site power line or none (BO-IND-13), or ODIN's reporting utilities show more than 50,000 meters out in a US state (BO-IND-14), a watched city's night lights fall 40% or more below its recent clear nights (BO-IND-15), or a US balancing authority's demand runs 25% or more below what its forecast implies for 3 hours or more (BO-IND-16).
warning_problems.issue_on_change: Publish each as an observation reported by its source. A judgment on cause (strike, weather or failure) needs a second independent line, such as Elements' weather or a suite tip of strikes on the same grid.
warning_problems.deactivation: The source reports power restored, or for the ZNPP two or more off-site lines available, for a US state 50,000 or fewer meters out at ODIN's reporting utilities, or for a balancing authority demand back within its own range.

hypotheses.title: Hostile action: strikes or sabotage on generation, transmission lines or substations
Weather, demand or equipment failure with no hostile act
Reporting gap or measurement artefact with no loss of power (a source not reporting, read late, or misread)

warning_problems.title: A national transport system stops: air traffic control, or an airline's own systems, halt US flights
warning_problems.watch_condition: The FAA's Command Center issues a ground stop for every airport, for a whole airline, at an airline's request at two or more airports within 2 h, or at an airport for an equipment or communications outage (BO-IND-17).
warning_problems.issue_on_change: Publish each as an observation reported by the FAA, quoting the condition it names. A judgment on cause (contractor fault, attack, power or a shared vendor) needs a second independent line, such as a provider's own incident (BO-IND-7) or onsets at several providers (BO-IND-8).
warning_problems.deactivation: The FAA cancels the ground stop or its effective time ends; the item stays 24 h after that.

hypotheses.title: Technical failure in the operator's own equipment or software, or a contractor's work on it, with no hostile act
Hostile action: a cyber attack on, or sabotage of, the system or what it depends on
An outside dependency failed: grid power, a telecom carrier, or a vendor many operators share (as CrowdStrike on 19 Jul 2024)

warning_problems.title: A service US daily life runs on stops working for its users, as the public or the press reports it (a bank, payments, an airline, a carrier, email, a government service)
warning_problems.watch_condition: Public Bluesky posts naming a watched service with an outage word surge against that service's own usual (BO-IND-18), or news headlines naming it with an outage word surge in GDELT (BO-IND-19).
warning_problems.issue_on_change: Publish each as an observation reported by the public or the press, never confirmed by the company, with the counts, the usual and links to the posts' own search or the articles. A judgment that the service is down needs the company's own word (a status page, BO-IND-7, or a statement) or both lanes at once with a second line such as an FAA ground stop (BO-IND-17).
warning_problems.deactivation: The count falls back under the line; the item ends when a run no longer finds the surge.

hypotheses.title: The service is failing for its users: an outage or a serious fault at the company or its systems
The surge is about something else: news of an outage elsewhere that names the company, a joke or meme, the words in another sense (a share price "down"), or the company's own denial
A dependency many services share failed (a cloud platform, a carrier, a payments network or a vendor), so several companies are reported at once
